maria.g: quick sync — i'm leaning toward switching our incremental bench anchoring to a small set of 'golden anchors' instead of running periodic full-suites. thoughts on tradeoffs?
kevin: i like the cost savings. main risks i see: anchors can drift and give false confidence, and cache/seqlen mismatch can hide perf regressions. we should bind anchors to model fingerprints.
alex: by anchors do you mean literally static prompts + expected metrics, or a sampled slice of live traffic?
maria.g: static curated prompts (<=200 per model family) + expected embeddings / latency / tok-cost bands. use them for smoke/regression and fast alerts :thinking_face:
lucy: operationally anchors are great for speed but can blind us to distribution shift. propose layered approach: anchors for fast alerts + stratified live-sample for coverage. also we need clear sampling config:
```
sampling:
  anchors: 150
  live_strata:
    - short: 0-64 (50%)
    - medium: 65-256 (30%)
    - long: 257-1024 (20%)
  cadence: incremental-5m
```
dave: can we bind anchors to model fingerprint (sha256) so we only re-anchor when model binary or tokenizer changes? fallback: nightly-mini-bench full run if fingerprints diverge.
kevin: +1 on fingerprint tie. also add seqlen buckets and kv cache state marker — otherwise kv warmup differences will skew anchor results. maybe a simple header like `kv_state: cold|warm` in the harness.
sre-bot: Deploy bot: nightly-mini-bench job updated (cron: 0 2 * * *). Current ETA for next run: 2024-07-18 02:00 UTC.
maria.g: action items: (1) i'll draft a proto sampling config PR (monday), (2) add fingerprint binding in model-registry (dave to help), (3) follow up RFC with explicit anchor/layered-sample policy. i'll open issues. :thumbsup:
